requirements.evidence: .env.example:1,7 sets APP_NAME=PegaFila / APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:21-23 pins all three; config/mail.php:122 'theme' => 'pegafila'; pegafila.css:651-658 puts #0f7490 on .button-primary (present in every action mail); lang/pt_BR.json:559 'Reset your password' and :804 'Verify your email address' added; routes/web.php:15-30 define the five named routes with guest group, throttle:6,1 on password.email and auth+signed+throttle on verification.verify; PasswordResetLinkController.php:31-33 always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')) whatever the broker returned; NewPasswordController.php:35-45 validates min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() + confirmed, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on id/hash mismatch) and redirects to '/'; reset view has a single email input.

conventions.evidence: Test-first coverage, CHANGELOG under [Unreleased] and docs/business-rules.md:137-143 kept in sync, PHPDoc on new public methods, Bulma markup with labels and role="status". Deviation: NewPasswordController.php:35-39 validates three fields inline although conventions call for a Form Request once rules go beyond one or two fields. CHANGELOG.md:12-13 inserts a stray blank line inside the Added list.

security.evidence: No account enumeration: PasswordResetLinkController.php:31-33 ignores broker status, including RESET_THROTTLED (tested in PasswordResetTest 'a throttled broker request does not reveal the user'); route throttles in routes/web.php:19,29; strong password rule plus confirmation; remember_token rotated (NewPasswordController.php:43); verification relies on signed URL + EmailVerificationRequest authorize; all view output uses {{ }} (e.g. reset-password.blade.php:28 token, :33 old('email', $email)); forceFill used only on server-controlled fields.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/MailThemeTest.php checks locale/name pins, theme config/file, rendered reset and verification mails (subject, PegaFila, Olá!, button, body, translated sub-copy, no 'having trouble clicking', #0f7490 inlined). PasswordResetTest.php covers guest-only redirect, sent/unknown same response, broker throttle, validation dataset, route 429, single email input, successful reset with remember_token rotation and event, invalid token, weak-password dataset, required token/email. EmailVerificationTest.php covers success+Verified event, wrong hash 403, other id 403, unsigned 403, throttle 429. Small gaps: no assertion that the mail links point to password.reset / verification.verify.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, built-in notifications and existing pt_BR.json strings; only two missing keys added. The two auth views (forgot-password.blade.php:1-16, reset-password.blade.php:1-16) duplicate the whole <head> including a CDN fallback, which is acceptable given layouts are out of scope but is copy-paste. The theme CSS copies Laravel's default theme wholesale (needed since a custom theme replaces the default).

readability.evidence: Small focused controllers with clear names (PasswordResetLinkController, NewPasswordController, VerifyEmailController); explanatory PHPDoc at PasswordResetLinkController.php:20-25; descriptive test names; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task; the welcome.blade.php:20-22 status notification supports the redirect-with-status requirement. User.php:15 now implements MustVerifyEmail, which the task did not ask for and has a side effect (the Registered listener will send verification mail once registration lands); defensible but slightly beyond scope. config/mail.php also re-adds the default 'paths' entry.

issues.explanation: Three-field validation is inline; conventions ask for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Implementing MustVerifyEmail was not requested and changes behaviour for future registration (automatic verification mail via the Registered listener).
The full HTML head with the Vite/CDN switch is duplicated across both auth views.
Mail tests do not assert that the action URLs are built from password.reset / verification.verify.
A blank line is inserted between list items under Added, breaking the list formatting.

review.summary: The change ships pt-BR defaults and phpunit pins, a pegafila mail theme with #0f7490 on the action button, the two missing JSON translations, a non-enumerating guest password-reset flow and a signed, throttled verification route, all backed by thorough Pest tests and updated docs. Remaining points are minor: inline validation where a Form Request is expected, an unrequested MustVerifyEmail on User, and some duplicated view boilerplate. I would approve with nits.
